parts.what: a match starting mid-stream caps it, and what was asked for comes back when the match ends
parts.seen: before: 2560x1440 at 30000 kbit/s; match "started": 1920x1080 at 12000 kbit/s, cap "LEAGUE MATCH", seen by the page 3708 ms later; match "ended": 2560x1440 at 30000 kbit/s, seen 3001 ms later; connection connected, 1 made (the engine looks for the game once a second and the page reads the PC's settings every 3 s, so a few seconds is expected)

parts.what: where FAST cannot run the page says so and draws NORMAL; the address can ask for either
parts.seen:
yes: opened with "?fast=refused&hold=1": 6 frames decoded, drawn NORMAL, and the panel says "FAST cannot run here (this browser was told to refuse it, as a test), so the picture is drawn NORMAL instead."
      yes: opened with "?drawing=normal&hold=1": 6 frames decoded, drawn NORMAL, and the panel says "This page's address asks for NORMAL (drawing=normal), so that is used whatever is chosen here."
      yes: opened with "?drawing=fast&hold=1": 8 frames decoded, drawn FAST, and the panel says "This page's address asks for FAST (drawing=fast), so that is used whatever is chosen here."

parts.what: FRAMES A SECOND on AUTO follows the viewer's screen, up to the PC's own

      yes: a pretended 144 Hz viewer on AUTO: the PC (whose own screen shows 180) sends up to 144 (wanted 144)
      yes: a pretended 240 Hz viewer on AUTO: the PC (whose own screen shows 180) sends up to 180 (wanted 180)
      yes: the panel shows [ AUTO ] pressed and says: "AUTO follows this screen. This screen shows 180 frames a second (measured here). The PC sends that many when its own screen and its limits allow."
